instantiated_cells.justification: Section 1-e(a)(1) exempts a lobbyist from filing a registration statement if in any year they do not expend, incur, or receive more than $5,000 in reportable compensation and expenses for lobbying, implying registration is required above $5,000.

Section 1-e(a)(1) sets a $5,000 threshold of reportable compensation and expenses for lobbying below which a lobbyist need not file a registration statement, so lobbyist-side expenditures above $5,000 trigger registration.

Section 1-h(b)(5)(ii) provides that expenses are listed in the aggregate if $75 or less, and detailed only if more than $75, establishing a $75 per-item itemization threshold on lobbyist bi-monthly reports.

Section 1-e(a)(1) states that a registration statement is not required for a lobbyist who does not exceed $5,000 in reportable compensation and expenses for lobbying in a year, creating a de minimis filing exemption threshold of $5,000.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled statute defines 'lobbyist' based on being retained/employed/designated and uses dollar thresholds, but contains no time-based (hours/days) definition of lobbyist/registration trigger.
No provision in the bundled text creates a filing exemption based on a percentage of compensated time devoted to lobbying.
